q: Which faucet suits outdoor and garden use?
n: A hose bibb is a faucet with a threaded nozzle for a hose, used outdoors and for gardens. Source: ASME A112.18.1; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: There are several reasons why soil stacks are not allowed in columns. Which of the following is NOT a reason?
o: The gas emitted will deteriorate the concrete
The size of the column will be too large
Cracks and leaks cannot be detected
Pipes will interfere with the reinforcing bars
n: Soil stacks are kept out of columns because they cut into the reinforcement, enlarge the column and hide leaks. Sewer gas deteriorating the concrete is not the usual reason. Source: NSCP 2015 (embedded pipes in concrete); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Which pipe carries discharge from water closets and similar fixtures?
n: A soil pipe carries discharge from water closets, urinals and similar fixtures (human waste). Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (definitions).

q: Which of the following should NOT be placed in line with a beam?
n: A water closet's large outlet and its 4-inch pipe cannot cross a beam, so it must not be placed in line with one. Lavatories and sinks have small drains. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines; structural coordination practice.

q: Which material is used for sanitary drainage pipes?
n: uPVC is the standard material for sanitary soil and waste drainage. PEX and PP are for supply, and GI corrodes. Source: ASTM D2665 (PVC DWV); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What is the typical drain and trap arm size for a sink?
n: Kitchen sinks typically take 1½–2 in. traps and trap arms. 2 in. is the common design size. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (fixture unit and trap size table).

q: How far back from a trench edge must excavated soil be kept, at minimum?
n: Excavated soil (spoil) must be kept at least 0.6 m (2 ft) back from the trench edge so it does not overload the side or fall in on workers. Source: DOLE OSHS Rule 1414 (excavation); OSHA 29 CFR 1926.651(j).

q: What is the minimum size of a floor drain cover?
n: Floor drain strainer (cover) plates are at least 4 in. × 4 in. (100 mm) in size. Source: ASME A112.6.3 (floor drains); manufacturer literature.

q: What wall panel gives access to valves and fittings?
n: An access panel is a removable wall or ceiling panel that gives access to concealed valves, cleanouts and fittings. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; manufacturer literature.

q: What is a recess in a wall for running pipes called?
n: A chase is a recess or vertical shaft in a wall or building for running pipes and ducts. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: If pipes are the "wires" of a plumbing system, what are the "switches"?
n: Valves control and shut off flow, the way switches control current. By opening, closing and throttling flow, valves let parts of the system be isolated for repair, just as switches isolate circuits. Source: Plumbing fundamentals.

q: Which fitting is used to turn a pipe run?
n: An elbow is the fitting that turns a pipe run (45° or 90°). Elbows come in 45° and 90° (short and long radius). Long-sweep bends are preferred in drainage to reduce clogging. Source: ASME B16.3.

q: What fitting changes the direction of flow?
n: An elbow changes the direction of flow. Tees and wyes branch it and reducers change its size. Source: ASME B16.3.

q: What is another term for a faucet?
n: A bibb (bib cock) is another term for a faucet, especially one with a threaded nozzle. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (definitions).

q: How are PPR pipes connected?
n: PPR (polypropylene random) pipes are joined by heat (socket) fusion welding, which melts pipe and fitting into one piece. Source: DIN 16962; PPR manufacturer installation guides.

q: What is the plain end of a pipe that fits into another pipe's hub called?
n: The spigot is the plain end of a pipe that slips into the bell (hub) of the next pipe. Source: CISPI Cast Iron Soil Pipe Handbook; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What is the trade name of a combination wye and 1/8 bend?
n: A "combo" is the trade name for a combination wye and 1/8 bend, which gives a long-sweep branch into a horizontal drain. Source: ASTM D2665 / CISPI fitting nomenclature.

q: What is the minimum area required for a toilet and bath (T&B) in a residential unit?
n: 1.20 m² is the commonly quoted minimum area for a residential toilet and bath compartment. Source: NBC IRR Rule VIII (room sizes); BP 220 IRR (minimum toilet area).

q: Who roughs in the sanitary pipes on site?
n: Sanitary rough-in (laying drain, waste and vent pipes before finishes) is done by the plumber, under a master plumber. Source: RA 1378 (Plumbing Law); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Who is in charge for plotting points and staking at the construction site?
n: Plotting points and staking are surveying tasks, done by the (geodetic or civil) engineer on site. Source: RA 8560 (Geodetic Engineering Act); construction practice.

q: What factor determines the vertical clearance required in a parking structure to allow vehicles to pass safely?
n: In parking structures, the lowest hanging pipes (sprinkler, drainage) usually set the clear height, so they decide the vehicle clearance. Source: NBC IRR Rule VII (parking clearances); NFPA 13 (sprinkler piping).

q: What is the tank used in a water closet?
n: A water closet's tank is the toilet tank (flush tank), which stores the flushing water. Source: ASME A112.19.2.

q: Which of the following is NOT commonly used in residential buildings?
n: Flushometers need large, high-pressure supply lines and are noisy, so homes use tank-type closets instead. Flushometers are for public toilets. Source: ASSE 1037; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What is the object located next to a kitchen sink and grease trap?
n: A catch basin is commonly placed outside, next to the kitchen sink's grease trap, to collect and settle the drained water before it goes to the drainage line. Source: Philippine plumbing practice; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: What is the tank that stores water for a toilet?
n: The toilet tank stores the water for flushing a tank-type water closet. When flushed, the tank's stored water drains through the flush valve into the bowl. A fill valve then refills it to the set level. Source: ASME A112.19.2.

q: What is an underground water storage tank called?
n: A water cistern is a tank for storing water, often underground. Septic tanks and grease traps handle waste. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (water storage).

q: Which water closet is designed to save water?
n: A dual-flush closet has a full flush for solids and a reduced half flush for liquids, saving water. Source: US EPA WaterSense; ASME A112.19.14 (dual-flush).

q: What is the typical flush volume of a low-flow urinal?
n: Low-flow urinals use about 1.5 L (0.4 gal) per flush or less. Source: US EPA WaterSense (urinals); Philippine Green Building Code (2015) water efficiency.

q: What is the typical flow rate for a kitchen sink, bidet, or lavatory (per minute)?
n: Low-flow kitchen, lavatory and bidet faucets are typically rated around 4.8 L per minute. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), water efficiency; US EPA WaterSense.

q: What is the flush volume of a single-flush tank-type water closet?
n: Standard single-flush tank-type water closets use 6 L (1.6 gal) per flush. Source: ASME A112.19.2; Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: What is the average flush volume of a dual-flush tank-type water closet?
n: High-efficiency dual-flush closets (6 L full, 3–4 L half) average about 4.8–4.9 L per flush. Source: US EPA WaterSense (HET 4.8 L); Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: Which shower head is ceiling-mounted?
n: A rain shower head is mounted on the ceiling (or a high arm) and drops water straight down like rainfall. Source: Shower fitting manufacturer literature.

q: Which bathtub material is the most expensive?
n: Enameled cast iron tubs are very heavy, durable and labor-intensive to make, so they are the most expensive of the choices. Source: ASME A112.19.1 (enameled cast iron fixtures); manufacturer price lists.

q: What must be finished before plumbing fixtures are installed?
n: Plumbing rough-in (concealed supply and drain lines, tested) must be finished before fixtures are set. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (inspection and tests).

q: What is the maximum number of fixtures, such as water closets, on one circuit vent?
n: A circuit vent may serve a battery of up to eight fixtures, such as water closets, on one horizontal branch. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (circuit venting); Uniform Plumbing Code.

q: What is the best orientation for a service area?
n: Service areas (laundry, utility, kitchen yard) are best placed on the south and west, where the hot afternoon sun dries laundry and shields the main living spaces. Source: Philippine tropical design guides; Olgyay, Design with Climate.

q: ABS stands for:
n: ABS = acrylonitrile butadiene styrene, a rigid thermoplastic used for drain, waste and vent (DWV) pipe. Source: ASTM D2661 (ABS DWV pipe).

q: Which of the following must be rectified on-site?
o: Water supply stub-out 500 mm from the floor
Height of water supply for female fixture aligned with water closet
Horizontal pipes aligned with vertical pipes
n: Horizontal supply pipes must not be run in line with (directly over) vertical risers in a way that blocks their access or required offsets, so that layout must be corrected on site. The other items are normal rough-in positions. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (installation); plumbing rough-in practice.

q: Which fixture is for washing the genitals and anus?
n: A bidet is a low basin fixture for washing the genitals and anus. Source: ASME A112.19.2 (vitreous china fixtures).
